cells.tense: You're reading the shape underneath things right now, and that read is steering what you reach for.
cells.ask: Pick one situation you keep circling and say the shape of it out loud to one person who wasn't there—just so it's shared.
cells.core: You look at something you care about and the structure shows itself: what connects to what, what holds, what's noise. That read doesn't stay separate from what you reach for. It tells you which direction is worth walking, and you walk it. Nothing needs arguing here, not with anyone and not with yourself. You're seeing clearly and you're pointed at something that's actually yours, and those two things happen to agree right now—that's the good part. It won't stay this clean, and this is what clean looks like. The next move isn't more reading. It's trusting what you've already spotted enough to keep moving. One thing, one person, said plainly, and you can carry the rest of the way on what you saw.

cells.tense: You're bracing against something that hasn't happened yet, and the shape you're tracking is turning into a threat report.
cells.ask: Pick one analysis you've been running and write down only what you can see from today, then put the pen down for the day.
cells.core: The pattern-spotting that usually serves you has gotten ahead of you. One connection leads to the next, and each one points at a flaw or a way this could fall apart. A version where you've finally outrun the trap keeps pulling you forward, and you follow, because up there it resolves. But it doesn't resolve, because the trap keeps moving. Meanwhile you're not walking toward what you want; you're auditing it. What you're reaching toward is still there and still good. You just keep stopping to check the ground. The next real move is small: read what's in front of you today, and stop at the edge of today. The rest of the territory can wait until you've taken one step.

cells.tense: You stand at the literal surface of things, and the deeper shape isn't being picked up right now.
cells.ask: Take one plain situation and ask it one question—what is this showing?—then leave it alone.
cells.core: You stay with what's practical. What's on the surface, what's said directly, what doesn't ask you to read between lines. That works—you get through, you don't lose footing. But the beneath-shape isn't being read, and the pull toward what you actually want has gone quiet with it. Quiet is wrong. It's still there. What's missing is the small move of asking a question of something that looks plain. Not everything, not as a practice. One thing, one question. That's the whole ask. Whatever the question turns up, you'll still be standing somewhere solid. The point isn't to see symbols everywhere, it's to let one thing be more than it looks for a minute, and see what you do with that. The answer can be mundane and still count.

cells.tense: You're making choices that follow a shape you haven't named, and you talk about it as just how things go.
cells.ask: Finish this line in a notebook: 'I keep noticing things go better when...'—then close it and go on with your day.
cells.core: There's a recurring shape in how things go for you. When you're at your best, what comes around again, what tends to work. You line your choices up with it. But you'd say it's just how things are, or a run of luck, or somebody else's doing. The pattern isn't hiding; it's just unclaimed. When you write the second half of that sentence down, what you've been following quietly can become something you follow knowingly. Not because the writing fixes anything, and not because you'd have to keep doing it. One line is enough. You don't need to understand where it came from, or prove it's real, or tell anyone. The shape holds either way, and now you'd know you're holding it too.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim in my draft is that patterns actively bind this person; the record shows a person who perceives pattern but doesn't acknowledge their own organizing role. A reader could say 'it's just overthinking, not pattern-vision' and it wouldn't matter—the mechanism still fits. The ask survives if my read is wrong because naming one repeated assumption is useful self-knowledge regardless. The sentence that serves me more than them is the abstract formulation about authorship; I've kept concrete and left it out of the core.
